You open a comm channel and faintly hear soldiers reporting to a superior. When the image resolves, the woman before you is wearing a general's insignia.

"The truth," General $personName says, noting your surprise, "is that our previous target is already gone. The problem now is procurement: a large armament order, and not one I can place through official channels. Bring me three mothballed Yoshura-class capital ships by whatever means you find acceptable. Are you interested?"

You take a moment to consider the unusual commission.

text:
"Excellent work." The aging general rests a hand briefly on your shoulder.

"Do you see that battlecruiser? The old hull is scheduled for transfer to Enigma III Industrial Station and dismantling within the month. Come with me. I want you to see it before it disappears."

You step onto a broad side deck. Dense turret clusters sit in rectangular groups near the centerline. The hull is clearly a Yoshura variant, but its unfamiliar paint scheme marks it as something you have never seen in any port registry.

A palm-sized holoprojector sits on the command room's long table. The compartment around it is dark and powerless, yet the device continues to project the bust of a man.

"Not a vessel of glory," she says. "A memory, given armor."

The general mutters the words while walking ahead, then turns sharply. The cybernetic eye on her right side locks onto you.

"The task you completed was a test. Before we speak of the real matter, there is something you need to understand."

---- You follow the general through a long, dim maintenance conduit and out through starboard airlock A ----

The noon glare forces you to narrow your eyes. Her voice cuts through it: "All of Enigma witnessed our love. Neither of us was ready to part, but the gender revolution had reached the point where no one could remain neutral." Her voice catches. "He always..."

"It was an expeditionary campaign, a large-scale struggle against the Hegemony. By the time full mobilization began at home, the vultures of war were already circling. Two fleets stalked each other for days along the asteroid-strewn edge of the system, easing their most aggressive formations into position. Maneuvers on that scale were a spectacle even by Sector standards. Detachments and scout wings stretched across three light-years.

"The first day went well. Battles ignited across four fronts, and the Hegemony vanguard took severe losses; one carrier-battleship was nearly reduced to scrap.

"The second day began with a mutiny. He led the defectors through an axial jump, seized a prototype Yoshura variant, and tore the campaign open from within."
options: 0:vft_continue:You cannot help leaning forward, eager to hear the rest.

text:
"After the battle, the traitors made no further move. They simply left the system. The Valkyrians never stopped looking for them." The general pauses, her expression unreadable.

"In truth, a report of possible fleet signatures near a certain system remained on my personal terminal until I retired from the front. That is where he is hiding. If command learns of it, treason and a gallows await him.

"This must end, but I will not see him dragged home in chains. That is why I found you. You are the only captain I believe has the patience and strength to handle him quietly. When it is done, every prize you take is yours."

After a longer conversation, you learn that he was once the refit chief aboard the general's flagship, obsessed with modification to an almost impossible degree.

"What do you think?" the general asks, her voice distant and unsteady.

text:
To your surprise, his comm request reaches you first. When you accept, he begins speaking as if he already knows why you came.

"You are the one she sent, aren't you? This day came later than I expected, but not by much."

The wanderer's eyelids droop. He looks less like a fleet commander than a man weathered by too many ports and too much empty space.

"Years in the void cost us dearly. This ship was once full of revolutionary hope. We tried to build our own utopia, but the colony bled fuel, food, and credit faster than we could replace them. Alliance merchants found every weakness in that fragile economy and squeezed until the people had nothing left."

"When I realized destroying trade fleets only made our own survival impossible, I understood what exile truly meant."
options: 0:vft_he_continue:"You once loved each other. How did it come to this?"

text: "At some point, communication simply stopped. Both sides insisted on justice through action, and neither could bear to speak first. On the eve of the great battle, my followers and I hid old carbines and electromagnetic rifles inside supply crates and moved them aboard. We could not let the chance pass. The weight of interstellar power was suffocating the movement. We had to reach the edge of Valkyrian force projection. It was our only road out."
options: 0:vft_he_continue:"I cannot deny that it was a great struggle."

text:
"We struck before anyone understood what was happening. Revolutionaries boarded a prototype Yoshura variant and killed the defending marine-lancers before the alarm could spread. Their pulse deflection fields failed under concentrated fire. The fall of that battleship became the movement's greatest achievement.

"The outpost was our final target. Once armed crowds stripped it bare, we broke from the organization and vanished into the silent void. From the captured battleship's frame and the outpost's secrets, I built this war machine. I chose to defend the meaning of my life with iron and blood until the final moment."

Resolve hardens in his eyes as he raises a hand to cut the channel.
options: 0:vft_he_continue:"Allow me one last question. What do you think of her now?"

text:
"She is the only one, in every moment."

Both sides fall silent. After a while, he looks at you, and the stars in his eyes seem never to have gone out. He cuts the connection with final resolve. The transmission ends, and the battle begins.

"I hate her."

The channel falls silent. The flagship shudders violently, and from beyond the bridge you hear someone shouting, "Incoming fire! Incoming fire!"

"From the moment we abandoned the organization, there was nothing left between us."

Static rolls through the channel, and the connection dies.
